title: Reduce latency for paginated top-k dashboard queries via index hints and partial result caching
creator: Evelyn Carter
description: Several dashboard endpoints that drive 'top N' lists and paginated tables show spiky 95th/99th latency under medium-to-high cardinality queries (multiple filters + wide time ranges). Current implementation relies on offset pagination over a heavy sort+join path and on-the-fly aggregation which causes repeated full-index scans and unstable tail latency. This ticket will implement index hints, keyset pagination where possible, and a partial result cache for frequently requested prefix pages to reduce backend CPU, DB read amplification, and latency tail for interactive console use.
background: Observed symptoms in dashboards: slow responses when users change time ranges or filter combinations; monitoring shows repeated identical queries from UI components (page 1 patterns) and heavy aggregate scans. Existing tickets addressed cursor and caching work on other paths (ENG-21104, ENG-24601), but we still see many endpoints using offset-based pagination and missing index usage for time-bucketed aggregates. UX reports and SRE alerts surface higher error budget consumption on console APIs during spikes.
proposed_solution: 1) Replace offset pagination with keyset (cursor) pagination for stable sorting columns (timestamp, score) for applicable endpoints; 2) Create compact materialized 'top_k_by_range' time-bucketed index table for tenant+route+metric dimensions to support efficient top-N queries across common time window sizes (1h, 6h, 24h); 3) Add explicit DB index hints and predicate re-ordering to ensure planner uses the time-bucket indexes; 4) Implement read-through partial-page cache (Redis) that stores the first 1-3 pages of frequently-requested queries keyed by a query fingerprint (tenant, route, filter hash, time-bucket, sort) with short TTLs and background invalidation on model or schema changes; 5) Provide transparent fallback to full aggregation when cache miss or when client requests deep pages; 6) Add feature flag and canary rollout for the new code path per-region/tenant.
design_decisions:
- Use keyset pagination with opaque cursor containing (sort_value, primary_key) encoded; avoid offset for pages beyond page 3 by disallowing deep offset queries in UI and providing export path for bulk retrieval.
- Materialized table design will be append-only per time-bucket and refreshed incrementally via a worker that consumes analytic event changes (CDC) to maintain near-real-time Top-K. Full rebuild nightly for correctness.
- Cache TTL default 30s for highly dynamic dashboards; configurable per-route. Use HLL to detect hot queries and extend TTL to 5m for repeat traffic.
- Keep migration reversible: new indexes and materialized tables created before switching read paths. Feature flag guards all new behavior.
implementation_plan:
- DB schema: add indexes and materialized top_k table (DDL scripts in repo).
- Worker: build CDC consumer to incrementally update materialized table (Rust service).
- API layer: implement keyset pagination helpers, query fingerprinting, and read-through cache wrapper.
- Telemetry: add metrics and traces for cache hit rate, query fingerprint distribution, db index usage, 95/99 latency per endpoint.
- Migrations and rollout: create indexes + table in staging, backfill recent windows, run canary for 5% of traffic, monitor, then promote gradually.
- Cleanup: deprecate offset endpoints and remove old aggregations after 2 sprints if stable.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy DB migrations to staging, run backfill job and smoke tests. 2) Deploy API with feature flag off. 3) Enable flag for internal tenants and run 24h soak. 4) Enable for 5% of production traffic (region A) with metrics alerting for latency/regressions. 5) Ramp to 50% then 100% if no regressions. 6) After 2 weeks, remove guards and schedule removal of legacy paths.
Fallback: if error rates or latency regress beyond threshold, roll back flag for the affected region.
metrics:
- Target latency: reduce 95th latency to <350ms for first page queries (was ~900ms for some filters).
- Cache hit rate target: >=60% for first-page fingerprints within first 24h deployment for hot dashboards.
- Reduce DB read ops per request by at least 3x for cached/optimized queries.
- Maintain error rate <0.1% during rollout.
- Add dashboards: per-endpoint 50/95/99 latency, cache hit ratio, top query fingerprints, index usage ratio.
acceptance_criteria: Keyset pagination implemented for targeted endpoints and verified via integration tests
Materialized time-bucket top_k table exists and is kept within 10s of real-time for new events in staging
Partial-page cache integrated with read-through behavior and configurable TTLs
Production canary shows decreased 95th latency for first-page queries by >=40% for monitored dashboards
No increase in 99th percentile error rate and DB CPU usage reduces or stays stable during canary
tasks: Write DDL for indexes and materialized top_k table
Implement CDC consumer to populate incremental materialized table
Add keyset pagination helpers and cursor encoding/decoding
Implement query fingerprinting and Redis read-through cache wrapper
Add feature flag and per-tenant rollout controls
Create integration and performance tests for new query paths
Instrument metrics and add console monitoring panels
Run staging backfill and validate correctness against current aggregates
Canary rollout and monitor for regressions
Cleanup legacy offset-based code paths after safe period
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Stale results due to cache TTL or backfill lag. Mitigation: conservative TTLs, visible 'last-updated' timestamp in UI and background revalidation for hot queries.
Risk: Increased write/maintenance cost for materialized table. Mitigation: incremental CDC updates and nightly compaction; limit dimensions to top-used filters (profile first).
Risk: Cursor incompatibility across sort variants. Mitigation: restrict keyset to stable sort columns and fall back to offset for unsupported sorts with explicit UI messaging.
Risk: Feature flag complexity causing divergent code paths. Mitigation: keep new path behind single flag and run automated smoke tests for both branches.
Risk: Redis cache thundering on invalidation. Mitigation: jittered TTLs, stampede protection with single-flight recompute lock per fingerprint.
notes: We should coordinate with the UX team to limit deep pagination in the UI and add 'export CSV' for full dumps. Also coordinate with Platform SRE to size Redis instance and DB index maintenance windows. Consider future work to generalize the materialized top_k table for other product surfaces.
